challengeFindings.title: A build loop pause on an unknown trend tells the owner "the limit is used up" when rounds are still left (Step 8 GATE_RERUN re-ask, Step 9 VERIFY_FIXED = 0 with a red gate, Step 12 GATE_RERUN re-ask)
The closing trendLine claims "and the code changed" when git could not tell (codeChanged: null: a missing parentSha or an unknown commit)
ciRoundMatches accepts a CI test-run row whose positive failures the selection does not back, so steps finish and the status-holes check pass a CI count no evidence holds

Two CI rounds from different CI generations of one run (attempt 1, then a re-run attempt 2) share scope ci:<run id>, so the trend compares their job counts and reads closing on a flaky re-run of the same commit

A step-done row whose free-text `scope` holds a line break plants a `Recommended:` or `Decision:` line in the `decisions compose --loop` Q1, and `decisions apply --by=headless` then takes the planted answer

A hand-appended CI `test-run` row can claim any positive failure count, and `ciRoundMatches`, `steps finish` and the completeness check accept it, because the count is the one evidence field never bound to the saved selection

challengeFindings.title: After the owner answers Try again at a used-up verify limit, counters grant raises the limit to 6 but PAUSE_MAX stays 3; a Step 9 round that fixes nothing on a red gate then composes --attempt=3 --max=3 and tells the owner "the limit is used up" with three rounds left
A resumed build that never held PAUSE_MAX composes --max= (empty); Number("") is 0, so every unknown-trend pause claims "the limit is used up" whatever the attempt
